chapter: Road life, segregation and band pranks
title: Musicians' hangouts: the Rhythm Club and neighboring bars
summary: Crawford lists the Rhythm Club and nearby bars where musicians met to talk.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: I wanted to ask you, too, did -- something I forgot to ask you the first time. Like, when the guys weren't working, like, during the day or something, where did they hang out? What kind of places? Were there many musicians' hang-outs that you remember, like in the '30s and '40s, or did you -

Oh, I'll tell you -- at the Rhythm Club, 130 -- right around the corner from Lafayette Theatre. They hung out at the Braddock Bar, and Dominick's Bar. That's where they hung out. Every day they had to be there. Just for their own curiosity. That's where they hung out. Alhambra Grill, places like that.
What did they do? I mean, like, --
So, like, were they just comparing notes
How different towns they'd been to.
